model.js:hash: Hash an explicit namespace/key to an unsigned 32-bit integer. This is reproducible simulation randomization, not cryptography; changing mixing or key order changes every downstream experiment.
model.js:draw: Return a uniform value strictly inside (0,1) from the keyed hash. Keep this separate from display hashes and never call it to animate or inspect a result.
model.js:generator: Supply sequential initialization draws within a dedicated namespace. Runtime choices instead use stable semantic keys so policy branches do not shift a shared RNG cursor.
model.js:gaussian: Box–Muller helper used by initialization gamma draws. It is a numerical sampler, not an empirical behavioral distribution.
model.js:gamma: Generate positive gamma variates for nine heterogeneous motive weights. Rejection/shape transforms consume only the initialization generator.
model.js:motives: Construct all nine social/economic/political × self/group/public weights and normalize them. Role/domain and beneficiary proportions are provisional priors; a motive is not a conduct classification.
model.js:validate: Normalize and reject unsupported setup values before constructing a world. Defaults, duration/repetition limits, override bounds and distinct policy IDs are part of the experiment contract.
model.js:conditions: Combine dated stored descriptors, bounded country baseline mappings and explicit user overrides. An override deliberately changes the reconstructed past as well as future conditions.
model.js:totalMoney: Sum every modeled cash account, including outside and unspent policy allocations. Use this conserved total rather than treating a bribe/fine transfer as newly created or destroyed money.
model.js:transfer: Execute a clipped conserved transfer without negative cash. Requested and actually paid amounts can differ, and unpaid ordinary costs are not silently created as debt.
model.js:requirements: Compute additional policy setup, recurring money and staff-time estimates. Cost tuples and GDP normalization are assumptions; this is not the existing institution’s entire budget.
model.js:createPopulation: Build the raw fixed 1,000-person society and its organizations, profiles, account structure and initial links. Its parameters mix sourced descriptors with explicit generic distributions; createInitial supplies the experienced starting state.
model.js:org: Create a simplified functional organization with capabilities, legal coverage, role practices and a leader/member roster. fn is one principal function, not a complete legal mandate description.
model.js:createInitial: Execute the dedicated twelve-month pre-policy reconstruction and preserve unfinished work/history. Reset intervention counters, not people, finances or cases; cache the identical state for matched comparisons.
model.js:initialDifference: Compare expected and imported starting states without replacing the imported values. Integers remain exact; only insignificant finite noninteger rounding and object-key order are tolerated.
model.js:validateInitial: Enforce initial schema, IDs, role counts, memberships, finances and exact reconstructed provenance. A plausible-looking JSON society is not accepted merely because its total population is correct.
model.js:constructor: Clone the supplied initial world, set the future-event stream/replicate, and create an observation sidecar before formal adoption. Only the reform branch adopts selected policies; baseline retains inherited arrangements.
model.js:index: Rebuild role/function/case lookup indexes after relevant transitions. These indexes accelerate access but do not create additional people or organizations.
model.js:emit: Append a tracked event/update without consuming world randomness. A tracking family can span case stages, resource reviews or a developing relationship.
model.js:cap: Aggregate operative capability among the relevant public functions, or inspect one organization. Capability is a bounded scenario quantity, not an empirical success probability.
model.js:recipients: Choose legally/functionally competent recipients and split reform funds using configured central/local shares. The shares are provisional country assumptions rather than measured budget allocations.
model.js:adopt: Enact the user-selected formal reform and its common intended scope immediately. This does not install implementation capacity, deliver teaching or bypass practical funding/work constraints.
model.js:effects: Keep all nine consequence slots explicit and finite. The returned vector is an assessed valuation used by utility, not a physical resource transfer.
model.js:choose: Score every available option under subjective motives, need, accountability expectations, TPB elements and keyed Gumbel uncertainty; take the maximum. Record meaningful opportunities only when a real alternative to a qualifying improper option exists.
model.js:operatingPolicy: Require active formal status, completed setup and recent delivery at the specific recipient. The check gates new personal exposure without erasing older memories or baseline capability.
model.js:expose: Deliver a real encountered policy episode with known source credibility and actual dose. Count additional teaching/verification contacts only when delivery is substantive and not a duplicate; uptake may still fail.
model.js:riskExperience: Attribute communicated procedure-specific cost information to one operative tool, falling back to ordinary experience. Avoid stacking the same event as generic risk and several policy bonuses.
model.js:practice: Read organization-and-role-specific honest/corrupt familiarity. This scalar affects particular effort/work expressions; its existence does not make repeated conduct an institution without reference reactions.
model.js:act: Complete the current meaningful choice or record an actual corrupt act, preserving the last-24 history. A one-option duty or repeated call cannot manufacture lawful recovery credits.
model.js:completeCorruption: Record one qualifying act and its participants, roles, amount, source organization and visibility. Victim payments are accounted separately; records can exist before any case or public allegation.
model.js:eligibleTool: Apply principal-function and covered-role gates. These are simplified modeled mandates and should not be presented as a comprehensive legal jurisdiction map.
model.js:coverage: Return current formal scope, with any endogenous narrowing applied. Formal scope can change before new delivery, so scope-sensitive diagnostics are capability estimates rather than proof of implementation.
model.js:covered: Use a fixed society/body/tool/person draw to keep legal coverage consistent over repeated encounters. Do not replace this with a fresh monthly compliance lottery.
model.js:operational: Combine legal coverage with actual organization capability, using a deterministic coverage gate for a specified person. This differs from the extra installed-delivery gate required for persuasive exposure.
model.js:relationship: Separate directional trust, shared membership, support affinity and effective access. Access can affect opportunity and insider incentives without providing automatic immunity.
model.js:experienced: Aggregate all service experiences into at most one bounded opinion/control update per person/month. Waiting files can increase actual burden without multiplying the learning rate indefinitely.
model.js:priorities: Rank work/funding requests by the actor’s evaluated priority-versus-defer utility difference. Ranking does not create additional money or time, and the later feasibility checks still bind.
model.js:policyFeedback: Compute observed delivery, governing support, resistance and waiting used in actor reviews. This is derived feedback, not a separately invented political-will coefficient.
model.js:peers: Select at most two accessible peers using directional relationship strength/trust. Sharing is selective and cannot broadcast omniscient world truth to the entire society.
model.js:fundingDependence: Measure recent active funder leverage relevant to the story subject using actual private flows. These private payments never replenish the public reform implementation pool.
model.js:tie: Look up a single undirected link record whose two trust fields remain directional. An absent record is not the same as absent organizational affinity.
model.js:related: Translate the modeled relationship-access threshold into a connected/outsider gate. This is an operational threshold, not a permanent class characteristic or legal finding.
model.js:link: Update useful/coercive ties and transmit a relevant reference’s approval/disapproval. Corrupt cooperation and coerced payment are distinct relationship kinds; neither repetition alone nor category membership establishes an institution.
model.js:nearest: Sample a small weighted candidate set using proximity, affinity and access, with possible remote contact. Despite the name it is stochastic weighted contact selection, not simply Euclidean nearest neighbor.
model.js:monthlyAccounts: Move ordinary income, organizational funding, modeled withholding and consumption through conserved accounts. Reset public staff budgets and record actual unmet-needs pressure; there is no endogenous GDP update.
model.js:scheduleWork: Reserve one finite public time budget across routine, reform and case categories using assessed priorities. Later operations debit both the relevant reservation and common remaining capacity.
model.js:fundPolicies: Disburse actually available treasury resources against each policy’s starting/current rate and setup/recurring requirement. Requested amounts can exceed mobilized funds, and policy order matters under scarcity.
model.js:implementPolicies: Execute actor-selected implementation/resistance/selectivity/diversion, shared-time/cash constraints and progressive setup. Apply only the operating tool’s named structural/learning hooks; full funding does not guarantee completion or integrity.
model.js:budgetReview: Run six-month utility/authorization decisions that can change rates, narrow scope or suspend a reform. Exceptional reviews, full repeal and reinstatement are not implemented by this routine.
model.js:addService: Create one persistent administrative request and count a contact once at arrival. Pending work is not silently counted as a newly arriving contact every month.
model.js:report: Let a witness/victim choose whether to report under subjective knowledge/safety and real costs. A submitted signal is not proof and can fail the affordability/viability threshold.
model.js:encounter: Separate proposer choice, counterpart response, extortion/refusal, prevention and physical completion. Only actual completed voluntary exchanges enter that category; extortion demands and victim payments have separate records.
model.js:encounters: Schedule role-specific opportunities in keyed random order, including campaigns and political pressure. These opportunity frequencies are generic model priors, not national encounter statistics.
model.js:processServices: Process prioritized requests with actual public staff/cash, preserving unresolved queues. Aggregate per-person experience once; completed waiting and unfinished waiting are distinct metrics.
model.js:makeCase: De-duplicate an underlying signal and assign its route, jurisdiction, evidence and next-stage date. A new file is not a guilty verdict or a newly created corrupt act.
model.js:audit: Spend finite scrutiny time on recent conduct records, with detection depending on actual covered capabilities and records. Include a lawful-control false-signal pathway and communicate notices separately from hidden detection truth.
model.js:responsible: Route a case stage to a configured competent function with explicit country exceptions. Fall-throughs and simplified mandates are intentional abstractions documented as limits.
model.js:processCases: Apply stage readiness, actual staff/money, controller choices and evidence thresholds before advancing or closing a case. Separate administrative/civil/criminal labels, proven findings, actual collections and unlawful adverse actions.
model.js:communicatedDecision: Update an accessed final decision once, using either one attributable operative policy or ordinary baseline-belief learning. A personally experienced decision cannot add a second public cost increment.
model.js:collectLiabilities: Collect only an existing assessed claim under cash, needs-buffer, per-month receipt cap and enforcement-resource constraints. Installments reduce debt and transfer money but do not create fresh sanction counts.
model.js:publish: Make an editor’s publish/withhold choice before spending publication funds and creating a claim/decision/correction record. Publication and announced decisions remain distinct from hidden model guilt.
model.js:information: Apply bounded attention, local/media exposure, credibility-weighted beliefs and selective social sharing. Descriptive conduct beliefs, reference expectations and objective truth are not interchangeable fields.
model.js:funding: Execute bilateral business-to-civic funding or withdrawal choices with actual private money. Dependence can change editorial conditions without mechanically buying compliance or funding public implementation.
model.js:changeEmployment: Move a person’s primary role/workplace membership while preserving identity, home, resources, history and ties. Count rotation only for an actual official-to-official organizational transfer.
model.js:organizations: Process constrained affiliation requests and periodic staffing/rotation. Requests with due=next month are still processed only at six-month organizational reviews, a documented effective delay.
model.js:politicalReview: Aggregate perceived conduct and affinity through the configured simplified election/appointment procedure. Update authority while retaining identity and history; this is not a national electoral forecast.
model.js:recover: Change the display state only after both the six-month no-new-act interval and three genuine completed integrity choices. The underlying conduct record and other agents’ reputations persist.
model.js:step: Execute the authoritative monthly order. Moving a call here can alter both causal timing and random-key identity even if each submodel remains individually correct.
model.js:classActivity: Summarize current-role agents’ last-24 meaningful opportunities. The denominator includes recorded attempted/uncompleted opportunities and is distinct from the common-encounter impact denominator.
model.js:macroDevelopments: Observe consequential treasury/service/pay, institution, public-disclosure and repeated-abuse developments. Notification thresholds do not themselves impose an extra behavioral corruption coefficient.
model.js:metrics: Read cumulative process counters and current collective states. A transfer, backlog stock, completed waiting total and true-conduct rate have different interpretations and must not be added as one welfare score.
model.js:record: Append ordinary metrics and an observation-sidecar snapshot after all monthly processes. Recording is passive; do not let reporting consume RNG or alter actors/accounts.
model.js:reporting: Expose the observation-only sidecar separately from the complaint report() method and simulation state. Initial-state/save compatibility remains governed by behavioral schema2.4.
model.js:diagnostic: Calculate explicitly labeled fixed-reference capability proxies or special realized indicators. This does not run independent empirical tests of institutions or consume simulation randomness.
model.js:assessment: Collect the twelve legacy diagnostic definitions. New reporting overrides for rolling merit/protection/penalty cohorts are a distinct documented readout path.
model.js:influential: Rank weighted network degree plus control/leadership leverage and retain eight people for detailed inspection. This is a heuristic power/centrality proxy, not all-pairs centrality.
model.js:view: Prepare a display payload with all people but detailed traits/traces only for highlighted actors. Keep display transformations separate from state; completion exports fuller records.
model.js:run: Advance until the configured duration using the same step() implementation. No alternative batch behavior or stochastic shortcut is introduced.
model.js:snapshot: Serialize simulation state, excluding observation and UI sidecars. Used to verify exact replay, import identity and documentation-only non-mutation.
model.js:assertInvariants: Fail loudly on population, balances, money conservation, staff double spending or invalid bounded profiles/history. These checks establish engineering consistency, not country realism.
model.js:comparison: Compare reform and baseline rate/quantity indicators with their own denominators. A null denominator remains unavailable; package impacts do not imply individual tool attribution.
adaptation.js:initialize: Construct each person’s stored trait baselines, current traits, expectations, motive anchors and learning memories using separate keyed draws.
adaptation.js:receptiveness: Compute component-specific uptake and conditional strength from actual individual traits, motives, knowledge, trust and own history. Credibility controls uptake; delivery quality later controls dose.
adaptation.js:observe: Deduplicate substantive episodes, draw uptake and magnitude separately, and apply declining new-learning caps plus bounded restoration. Rejected delivery still advances the exposure counter; it is not successful learning.
adaptation.js:influence: Sum retained eligible component levels and targets, applying context gates and cross-policy bounds. A non-targeted component must not receive a generic bonus.
adaptation.js:decision: Adjust only the relevant attitude, norm and feasibility elements for the specific option/context. Actual resources, consent and law are still checked by the engine after intention.
adaptation.js:advance: Apply wear-off, bounded trait/motive evolution and ordinary risk relaxation exactly once per elapsed month. Never erase conduct or restore an integrity icon through this learning update.
adaptation.js:accountability: Learn from one personally experienced or accessed announced decision with bounded prior-relative targets. Deduplication and forgetting limits are explicit and do not reveal hidden truth.
adaptation.js:incomeExperience: Learn expected lawful receipts from one actual monthly observation, including supplements. It is separate from measured unmet-needs pressure and from new money creation.
adaptation.js:work: Improve skill only through performed work, with a ceiling relative to initial skill. This is not an instant expertise gain from selecting a policy.
adaptation.js:knowledge: Read context-specific usable knowledge from baseline and retained component influence. Reporting-channel instructions are not universal knowledge for unrelated conduct.
adaptation.js:safety: Read subjective reporting safety from experienced baseline and retained target-specific learning. Do not replace it with omniscient true protection capacity.
adaptation.js:refresh: Refresh derived knowledge/accountability expectations from retained memories without double-counting generic gains.
adaptation.js:feedback: Record bounded experienced/enacted salience and credibility feedback used for slow future adaptation; no conduct classification occurs here.
adaptation.js:summary: Export interpretable numerical traits, retained influences and exposure histories for inspection. Summary values are model traits rather than validated psychological scores.
adaptation.js:valid: Validate complete stored numerical psychology, memories and bounds for initial/final profiles.
adaptation.js:validSummary: Validate the smaller inspection-summary structure accepted in completed saved results.
adaptation.js:messageRate: Scale accessed information by credibility and the recipient’s openness/learning. This does not guarantee acceptance of a true or false claim.
adaptation.js:context: Map action names to the policy-learning contexts actually used by decision(). A new action name needs an explicit context review.
reporting.js:init: Capture conditions before adopt() and inherit the separately archived pre-policy observations. Keep the monitor outside state and separate from the complaint report() method.
reporting.js:activity: Accumulate an actual delivered process hook only; selecting a policy or inspecting a panel cannot create output.
reporting.js:remember: Cache a cloned pre-policy observation archive keyed to the starting society without changing its serialized state.
reporting.js:sample: Read all policy-specific snapshot conditions and explicitly defined outcomes. Estimated capability, rolling realized ratios and matured violation cohorts remain distinct.
reporting.js:record: Update passive counters/snapshots and a bounded real-event evidence index after the monthly world update. Protect important per-policy records from last-200 feed truncation.
reporting.js:windowValue: Subtract cumulative observed activities at equal month boundaries, including the inherited year. Never compare an opening queue stock with a year of activity or average unweighted monthly rates.
reporting.js:eventsFor: Select existing records no later than the review month, prioritizing material implementation changes. Package impact uses the whole package independently of the policy selector; contextual connections do not identify causes.
reporting.js:interpret: Choose a predefined statement from measured levels/direction/missingness. Precision thresholds are not significance tests; no anecdote or causal explanation is generated from hidden assumptions.
reporting.js:outcomeMeta: Name the rolling observed reporting overrides so they cannot be confused with the older aggregate diagnostic definitions.
reporting.js:valid: Validate optional saved observation histories, numeric fields, IDs and bounded event metadata. Absence in an older completed save is reported honestly rather than filled with invented data.
reporting.js:view: Return the observation payload without recomputing actor decisions or consuming simulation draws.
app.js:getConfig: Read and validate draft setup independently of an active run. Source values, user overrides and initial/future seeds retain separate meanings.
app.js:initializeWorker: Start a fresh paired experiment and reset historical-review selection; use a new event seed unless exact replay was requested.
app.js:renderPolicyAssessment: Connect one selected policy’s outputs/outcomes with the package impact, same-month baseline and fixed pre-adoption snapshot. Rendering must remain passive and preserve the real measurement windows.
app.js:reportMeaning: Insert an escaped predefined interpretation with at most two real linked records and expandable additional developments.
app.js:showReportEvent: Open an existing tracked record and its available updates in place, then highlight participants without rerunning the model.
app.js:reportChart: Draw observational series and a shared review-month marker; impact uses paired difference against zero rather than an overlapping pair of cumulative curves.
app.js:renderAssessment: Coordinate the new stage panels with expandable full-package quantities and repetition summaries. Package totals remain separate from tool-specific conditions.
app.js:validatePayload: Validate untrusted JSON data and preserve exact starting-state identity; never execute imported content. Monitoring is optional for older2.4 results but checked when supplied.
app.js:loadPayload: Stop execution, reset review state and load for inspection only. Existing completed results do not gain missing monitoring data without a rerun.
app.js:payload: Serialize setup, exact initial society and matching completed results. This is a scenario/result backup, not an in-flight checkpoint.
app.js:drawMap: Project observed conduct/affinity/network data for display without changing physical geography or simulation RNG.
app.js:inspector: Explain why a highlighted actor matters and show recorded choices plus numerical learning. Perceived intentions and completed acts remain distinct.
app.js:storeAction: Persist named scenarios on device with IndexedDB and localStorage fallback, reporting failures instead of silently promising durable storage.
app.js:csv: Escape CSV values and guard formula-like string cells. CSV quantities retain their named units and are not a substitute for the full JSON state.
worker.js:makePair: Construct reform and no-new-reform baseline from the exact same initialized state and replicate identity.
worker.js:finishPair: Check invariants, retain the first visible trajectory, export complete records and summarize repetitions. Simulation ranges are not empirical confidence intervals.
worker.js:pump: Schedule bounded batches without changing monthly step order or random streams; pause/pace affect responsiveness only.
visualization.js:projection: Compute deterministic analytical layout using conduct radius, affinity and bounded local collision/cooperation forces. Do not mutate physical locations or world randomness.
visualization.js:impactWindow: Calculate interval counts before dividing, preserving each branch’s denominator. Missing observations return unavailable rather than manufactured zero.
visualization.js:impactSeries: Align paired months and their chosen rate windows. An absent corresponding observation cannot be treated as a zero-effect month.
visualization.js:impactDifference: Keep a tiny nonzero effect visible with three decimals or scientific notation; formatting precision is not empirical accuracy.
baseline.js:organization: Map stored descriptors/narrow instrument observations to bounded provisional coverage/capability priors. Missing evidence is not absence of national safeguards.
baseline.js:conditions: Rescale distinct dated political proxies and keep unmeasured cultural fields as explicit neutral editable assumptions.
run-seeds.js:prepareRun: Preserve exact replay seeds when requested and otherwise assign a fresh future-event identity without redrawing the starting society.
